title: Isabella oncall scratchpad - 2026-03-09
content:
2026-03-09 Oncall scratchpad (Isabella)
--------------------------------------------------
Summary:
- 02:12 UTC: Pager (P1) - elevated 5xx rate and p95 latency for /v1/generate (hosted-api).
- Symptoms: p95 ~1.1s, 5xx rate peaked ~6% for ~8 minutes. Autoscaler triggered burst workers; partial fallback to smaller model enacted by fallback-policy.
- Mitigation: manual routing to region-us-west-2 fallback pool at 02:20 UTC. Error rate/latency back to baseline by ~02:25 UTC. Declared resolved ~02:30; monitoring for recurrence.

Pager timeline:
- 02:12: Alert triggered (p95 > 800ms for 3m)
- 02:14: Page to me (Isabella)
- 02:16: Triage - checked latency dashboards, pod restarts, GPU memory metrics
- 02:18: Noted spike in pod restarts on node gpu-uc-13 (OOMKilled entries)
- 02:20: Manual routing to fallback pool applied
- 02:25: Metrics stabilized; continued monitoring
- 02:30: Incident declared resolved (monitoring window ongoing)

Initial findings / hypothesis:
- Multiple model-serving pods on gpu-uc-13 were OOMKilled. Infra shows a kernel-level upgrade deployed to that node pool ~01:50 UTC. Hypothesis: kernel update + memory fragmentation increased memory pressure, exacerbated by a burst of large batch requests.
- Autoscaler did scale, but new pods landed on same problematic node pool due to default scheduling; fallback model prevented wider customer impact.

Immediate follow-ups (48h):
- ACTION: Add node-level kernel-update check to pre-deploy gating for infra rolling updates. Owner: Priya Shah. Due: 2026-03-12.
- ACTION: Create alert for repeated OOMKills per node within a 10m window (current alerting is per-pod). Owner: Noah Chen. Due: 2026-03-11. JIRA: SRE-4123.
- ACTION: Adjust autoscaler policy to prefer spreading across node pools when GPU memory pressure is detected. Owner: Isabella Ross. Due: 2026-03-15.
- ACTION: Add runbook step to route traffic to fallback pools and rollback kernel updates if correlated failures detected. Owners: eng-serving-runtime + release-engineering. Link runbook PR in postmortem.

Runbook TODOs (quick wins):
- Update "gpu-node-health" runbook: add kernel-upgrade checks and instructions to inspect dmesg for OOM killer evidence.
- Update "fallback-routing" doc: document manual routing CLI commands, verification steps, and safety checks.
- Create post-incident checklist template for P1 latency incidents. Owner: Mia Li.

Debugging artifacts / notes:
- Node logs (gpu-uc-13): dmesg contains multiple "Out of memory" and process killed entries around 02:15 UTC. Saved to /tmp/incident-2026-03-09/gpu-uc-13-dmesg.txt.
- K8s events: rapid pod evictions, scheduling delays; kubelet reported "eviction threshold breached" on that node.
- Model-serving logs: several pods show runtime assertion during KV cache allocation immediately before OOM. Could be leak or sudden increase in batch size.
- Slack: #oncall-incidents thread (see linked_artifacts) has live timeline and commands used.

Open questions:
- Any anomalous traffic from a single customer during the window? (Ticketed to SRE + Support to query usage logs)
- Did release-engineering push any kernel/driver updates? Confirm with infra team (Priya).

Post-incident meeting actions:
- Draft post-mortem with timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation effectiveness, and action items + owners. Owner: Isabella. Draft by 2026-03-11.
- Reproduce memory fragmentation scenario in staging (eng-serving-runtime). Owners: devs on-call + Solutions Eng.
- Validate fallback policy for multi-region failover with ops test. Owner: Platform Eng. Due: 2026-03-16.

Personal quick TODOs:
- Link runbook PR (github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8791) in postmortem.
- Ping release-eng in morning to confirm kernel roll plan and any follow-ups.
- Add tiny bash snippet to runbook for grabbing dmesg + recent pods and uploading to /tmp/incident-<date>/ for quick artifact collection.

Sample log snippets:
- "Out of memory: Killed process 42819 (redwood-server) total-vm:3123456kB, anon-rss:2987652kB"
- "kubelet: eviction threshold breached, freeing memory by evicting pods"

Retrospective notes:
- What went well: fallback routing prevented customer-visible downtime beyond elevated latency; mitigation was applied quickly.
- Improvements: runbook gap around kernel-update correlation and autoscaler spread policy; alerting granularity for node-level OOM patterns.

I'll file the postmortem skeleton tonight and assign action items. Watch for alerts in the 02:10-02:40 window over the next 72h for any recurrence.

-- Isabella Ross
